//region: EMPTY = whole genome. This is the mode the cohort run uses.
//phased_vcfs: The chr20 PER-SAMPLE file from the split, as a one-element array. This is the first run on genuinely single-sample input, so the task should report 'already single-sample; skipping the subset' -- the 22.2 min phase, 28% of the previous run, disappearing rather than shrinking. Still chr20 only, so loci elsewhere remain insufficient_reads; swap in all 22 once the split finishes and make_trgt_phase_table.py --split-base has filled the columns.
//phased_vcf: Still the chr20 MULTI-SAMPLE callset, because the per-sample split does not exist yet. Consequence: only chr20 reads get haplotagged, so loci on other chromosomes resolve as insufficient_reads. That is expected for this run and is not a failure.
//cpu: 8 parallel haplotag workers. whatshap is single-threaded and sat at 1.01 of 6 cores for the whole of the first run, so this is the lever. The floor is the largest contig (~8% of reads), not total/N, so past about 12 there is nothing left to win.
//memory_gb: 16, not 32. Measured peak was 1.02 GiB; eight concurrent whatshap workers want roughly 8. 16 also keeps the request under GCE's 6.5 GB-per-vCPU cap at 8 vCPU, so cpu=8 is honoured exactly -- 32 GiB with cpu=4 silently billed 6 vCPU on the first run.
//haplotag_jobs: 0 means use cpu. Set it lower only to debug a worker.
//disk_gb: Deliberately ABSENT so the WDL default applies: ceil(2.8 * size(bam,'GB')) + 80, which is 136 GB at 19.79 GiB. Setting it here would re-freeze the guess this replaced.
//preemptible: 0 while the runtime is still being measured. Once parallel haplotag brings the task under an hour, preemptible becomes worth revisiting for the cohort run.
